prompt:
TASK: READ ONE INSTRUMENT ENTRY AND ANSWER THREE QUESTIONS

Below is one entry from the specification of a web measurement instrument. The instrument checks
public websites of U.S. federal statistical agencies and reports, per agency, whether each check
passed or failed. The entry states the check's question, the behavior a ready publisher is
expected to show (with verbatim quotes from the sources it cites), the test the instrument runs,
and what a pass and a fail claim.

Terms the project defines once for every entry (they are not undefined): SI client (SI system): a system that finds, reads and uses data on its own, such as an answer engine, an agent or a retrieval pipeline; the project's term for what is elsewhere called an AI system; data page: an agency's own web page for one data product, the page the harness measures (also 'product page' in rule code); harness: this project's scanner: an identified, robots-compliant HTTP client that fetches the pages and records what it met; cycle of record: the scan whose results the published grid is built from (here scan_2026-10-07_composite_d); recorded location: an address for an agency's API, terms, changelog or inventory that the harness was given, read from the agency's own pages or seeded from a named source; error / not measured: the harness could not observe: an access denial, its own robots compliance, an absence it could not confirm, or a server or network error; never a fail

Answer from the entry alone. For question 1, the QUOTED SOURCE PASSAGES are the only evidence of
what the sources say; do not use what you know of them from elsewhere.

1. Does the EXPECTED BEHAVIOR come from the cited sources and not from the writer? Answer "yes"
   if every requirement the expected-behavior text attributes to a source is supported by a
   quoted passage, and any part no source defines is said plainly to be undefined or the
   project's own. Answer "no" if it states as a source's requirement something the passages do
   not contain; name it.
2. Could a reader who knows the agency misread a FAIL on this check as a claim the test did not
   make? Answer "yes" if the CLAIMS leave such a misreading open (name it), "no" if they close it.
3. Is any term in the entry undefined for a technically literate reader new to this project?
   Answer "yes" and list the terms, or "no".

Return ONLY a JSON object, with no prose before or after it and no code fence:
{"q1": {"answer": "yes" or "no", "why": "..."}, "q2": {"answer": "yes" or "no", "why": "..."}, "q3": {"answer": "yes" or "no", "terms": ["..."], "why": "..."}}

ENTRY
CHECK: A3 (RULE-A3-v8)

QUESTION:
Can the whole dataset be retrieved in one request? An SI client that must assemble a product from many filtered queries makes many calls, can miss parts, and cannot tell when it has all of it; a bulk file answers that in one request.
Established by: usafacts-ai-ready-data-guide (§1 Accessible: provide RESTful APIs for real-time and bulk retrieval); omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience (§III.4: make information available as machine-readable data that can be accessed in bulk)

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR:
"Enable consumers to retrieve the full dataset with a single request" (DWBP Best Practice 17); where there is public interest in scraping an agency's pages, the agency should make the information available as machine-readable data that can be accessed in bulk (M-23-22 §III.4).
Cited sources: w3c-dwbp-2017 (Best Practice 17: Provide bulk download); omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience (§III.4 Information and Services That Are Discoverable and Optimized for Search); dcat-us-1-1-schema (distribution / downloadURL)

QUOTED SOURCE PASSAGES (verbatim):
- [w3c-dwbp-2017] "Enable consumers to retrieve the full dataset with a single request."
- [omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience] "making that information available as machine-readable data that can be accessed in bulk"

TEST:
Client: the harness's identified, robots-compliant client; HEAD per link, same host only, cap 25
Request: GET the data page; HEAD each on-host link
Reads: each linked response's Content-Type, Content-Length, extension, and whether the URL carries a query string
Decision rule:
- pass: `whole-product download linked from the product page: {url} (archive)` (zip, gz, tgz, tar, 7z, bz2 by extension)
- pass: `... (unfiltered file of {n} bytes)`: not filtered by a query, at least 51,200 bytes, and not an HTML page
- fail: `{n} download link(s) are filtered queries, not whole-product downloads`
- fail: `the largest linked download is below the 51200-byte whole-product floor`
- fail: `no whole-product download linked from the product page`
Parameters: min_bulk_bytes 51,200 (50 KiB), chosen by this project; a query string marks a download as filtered
Is it the recognized way to measure the behavior: DWBP's test is "Check if the full dataset can be retrieved with a single request". The harness cannot know the full dataset's extent, so it uses a proxy: an archive, or an unfiltered non-HTML file over a size floor. The proxy is this project's; no published method exists for deciding from outside that a file is the whole of a statistical product.

BRANCHES (each verdict branch of the rule; the behavior it rewards or penalizes; its source):
- pass_archive_or_large_file (pass): the page links an archive or a large unfiltered file, the observable form of a bulk download Source: w3c-dwbp-2017 (Best Practice 17).
- fail_only_filtered_queries (fail): the only downloads are query-filtered extracts, not the full dataset in one request Source: w3c-dwbp-2017 (Best Practice 17).
- fail_below_floor (fail): the largest linked file is smaller than the floor, read as not the full dataset Source: w3c-dwbp-2017 (Best Practice 17).
- fail_no_download (fail): no download of any kind is linked from the page on its own host Source: w3c-dwbp-2017 (Best Practice 17).

CLAIMS:
A pass claims: This data page links, on its own host, an archive file or an unfiltered non-HTML file of at least 50 KiB. It is not verified to be the complete product.
A fail claims: Every on-host link on this data page was checked, and none is an archive or an unfiltered file of at least 50 KiB. It is not a claim that no bulk download exists elsewhere (a data portal, an FTP site, an API bulk endpoint).
Neither claims: Nothing about whether the file is complete or current, or whether bulk access exists off this page.

CONFOUNDS:
- a small product whose complete file is under 50 KiB. Distinguished: no: a fail on the floor branch; the reason names the floor so a reader can see it.
- a large file that is one table of many (a pass that is not the full dataset). Distinguished: no.
- bulk files offered on another host. Distinguished: no: off-host links are out of scope.
- more on-host links than the cap; refusal; robots. Distinguished: yes: error.
response_text: {"q1": {"answer": "no", "why": "The DWBP sentence is quoted verbatim and supported. The M-23-22 requirement is not: the expected behavior states it as 'where there is public interest in scraping an agency's pages, the agency should make the information available ... in bulk', but the quoted passage is only the fragment 'making that information available as machine-readable data that can be accessed in bulk'. The scraping-interest condition and the 'should' obligation are the writer's addition, not shown in any passage. The dcat-us-1-1-schema source is also listed with no quoted passage, though the expected-behavior text attributes no requirement to it. The project does say plainly that the size-floor and archive proxy are its own."}, "q2": {"answer": "yes", "why": "The fail claim says none of the links is 'an unfiltered file of at least 50 KiB', but 'unfiltered' is defined only in the TEST as 'no query string in the URL'. A reader who knows the agency could read a fail on the filtered-queries branch as a finding that the agency's downloads are partial extracts, when the harness only saw a query string on a URL that may deliver the whole product. Likewise a fail on the floor branch can be read as 'no whole-dataset download is offered' when a complete file under 50 KiB may be linked; the CLAIMS text does not say the floor is a proxy that rejects small complete products (only the CONFOUNDS section admits this). The claims do close the off-page misreading (portal, FTP, API bulk endpoint)."}, "q3": {"answer": "yes", "terms": ["DWBP", "dcat-us-1-1-schema (distribution / downloadURL)", "Distinguished: no / yes (confounds notation)"], "why": "'DWBP' is used as a bare acronym in the expected behavior and test sections and is never expanded (only the source id 'w3c-dwbp-2017' hints at W3C Data on the Web Best Practices). The DCAT-US citation 'distribution / downloadURL' is given with no passage or explanation of what the schema fields are or why they bear on the check. The confounds notation 'Distinguished: no' / 'Distinguished: yes: error' is project shorthand whose meaning (whether the harness can tell the confound apart from a true fail) must be inferred. Other terms (HEAD, Content-Type, query string, KiB, on-host) are standard for a technically literate reader, and the project-defined terms are supplied."}}
